title: Photosynthesis
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Photosynthesis Worksheets (Word Equation, Leaves, Starch Test)
standard_code: KS3 Biology: Material cycles and energy
standard_text: The reactants in, and products of, photosynthesis, and a word summary for photosynthesis; the dependence of almost all life on Earth on the ability of photosynthetic organisms, such as plants and algae, to use sunlight in photosynthesis to build organic molecules that are an essential energy store and to maintain levels of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere; the adaptations of leaves for photosynthesis; the role of leaf stomata in gas exchange in plants; plants making carbohydrates in photosynthesis and gaining mineral nutrients and water from the soil via their roots.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on photosynthesis: the word equation, chloroplasts, leaf adaptations, stomata, the starch test, the rate of photosynthesis and minerals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
key_sub: Light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll; oxygen is given off.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants make their own food by photosynthesis.

  • carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll in chloroplasts).
  • Leaves are broad and thin, with stomata for gas exchange and palisade cells full of chloroplasts.
  • Light, carbon dioxide and temperature affect the rate. Plants also need minerals such as nitrates from the soil.
Example

Lamp moved further away. Rate?

Less light

Answer: slower

Example

Is oxygen a reactant or a product?

Look at the equation

Answer: a product

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking oxygen is an input.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.

faq.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen. Light energy is needed and is absorbed by chlorophyll.

faq.q: How do you test a leaf for starch?
faq.a: Boil it in water, warm it in ethanol in a water bath to remove the chlorophyll, rinse it, then add iodine. Blue-black means starch.

faq.q: What affects the rate of photosynthesis?
faq.a: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature. The one in shortest supply limits the rate.

c: a waste that stops the reaction
items.e: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy.

items.q: What are stomata?
c: tiny holes in a leaf that let gases in and out

items.e: Light energy comes from the sun and is captured by chlorophyll.

items.q: Harry lists the parts of photosynthesis. Is carbon dioxide an input or an output?
items.e: Carbon dioxide comes from the air and enters through tiny openings in leaves (stomata).

items.q: Which mineral do plants need for healthy roots?

items.q: Leaves have veins (xylem and phloem). How does this help the leaf?
c: Carbon dioxide only has a short distance to diffuse to the cells.
They bring water and carry away sugars.
Carbon dioxide can diffuse in and oxygen can diffuse out.
They have a large surface area to absorb light.

items.q: Grace asks where carbon dioxide fits in photosynthesis. Which is true?
c: It stores energy and is used as food and building material.
It comes from the sun and is captured by chlorophyll.
It comes from the air and enters through tiny openings in leaves (stomata).
It is released into the air through the leaves.
items.e: Carbon dioxide comes from the air and enters through tiny openings in leaves (stomata).

items.q: Leo reads about an experiment: a tree planted in a pot gained 70 kg in 5 years, but the soil lost only 2 kg. Where did most of the tree's mass come from?
c: carbon dioxide from the air (and water) turned into sugar by photosynthesis
items.e: This is like van Helmont's experiment: the carbon in a tree comes from carbon dioxide in the air.

items.q: Which mineral do plants need to make chlorophyll?
Ruby asks where water fits in photosynthesis. Which is true?
c: It is released into the air through the leaves.

It comes from the soil through the roots.
items.e: Water comes from the soil through the roots.

items.q: Guard cells surround each stoma. How does this help the leaf?
c: They bring water and carry away sugars.
They open and close the stoma to control water loss.
They can absorb lots of light for photosynthesis.

items.q: Kai covers half of a leaf with foil for two days, then tests the leaf for starch with iodine. Only the uncovered half turns dark blue-black. What does this show?
c: Light is needed to make food (sugar and starch).
Leaves make food in the dark.

items.q: Palisade cells are near the top of the leaf. How does this help the leaf?

They open and close the stoma to control water loss.
Gases can move easily between the cells.
